To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the fraction of total rock content that is easily accessible to acidic aqueous solutions is strongly dependent on the intensity of mineralogical alteration, (2) during retrogression of paragneisses and associated metabasites at the KTB site in southern Germany, considerable fractions of many major and trace elements are mobilized in situ, and (3) the whole-rock element composition is preserved during retrograde alteration, suggesting low fluid/rock ratios and low flow rates.

during retrograde metamorphic alteration, the whole-rock contents of elements are maintained, whereas the leachability of some elements increases and the leachability and whole-rock content of other elements decreases.

(a) the easily leachable fraction of many elements is considerable in retrogressed paragneisses and metapelites of the KTB drill core; (b) the easily leached fraction of elements increases with the intensity of retrograde metamorphism; and (c) the whole-rock content of many elements was maintained during retrograde metamorphic alteration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mobility of elements in a retrogressively metamorphosed, highly sheared, metapelitic rock.
element mobility in the KTB drill core samples and with the changes in element leachability during retrograde metamorphic alteration.
the mobility of major, minor, and trace elements in retrogressed paragneisses and metamorphosed metabasites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
element mobility in the studied rocks is low, but not negligible.
element redistribution during retrogression was limited to a few meters.
the mobility of elements during retrograde metamorphic alteration in the KTB paragneisses is governed by the mineralogic composition of the rocks and the intensity of mineral alteration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the studied rocks were altered by a fluid that was not only acidic but also reducing, and that the fluid/rock ratio was low.
the studied samples were altered by retrograde metamorphism in a closed system, with only minor element transport and no significant element losses.

element redistribution during retrogression of the paragneisses and their contact with metabasites was restricted to the meter scale, and was mainly controlled by the intensity of mineralogical alteration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobility of elements in the retrograde metamorphic environment is controlled by the mineralogy of the rock, the intensity of alteration, and the whole-rock content of the elements.

, in spite of the high mobility of many elements during retrogressive alteration, element transport was limited on a meter scale and that, therefore, the whole-rock composition of the KTB paragneisses is not significantly affected by alteration.
the easily leachable fractions in the studied samples reflect the degree of retrograde alteration.
